subject: Postmortem packet and traceable commitments — Aurora throughput spike
messages:
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Subject: Aurora throughput degradation — initiating RCA & customer readout

Team — FYI: Aurora hit a sustained throughput degradation on 2027-04-07 between 21:40-23:05 UTC that impacted tail latency and scaled error rates for a subset of production routes (embedding+generate). The customer reported timeouts and a high error rate on their peak checkout window; they engaged their executive sponsors.

I'm starting the RCA packet and will coordinate the customer-facing readout. Ben/Karthik, please pull scheduling/agent logs and the autoscaler telemetry (GPU util, queue depth) by EOD PT. Laura, I anticipate we'll need an exec-level summary and a recommended customer credit.

Initial ask list:
- Produce a draft RCA (root causes, timeline, mitigations) by EOD Fri 2027-04-09.
- Targeted mitigation: canary with conservative batching/disabled KV-cache for suspect model variant; rollout plan within 72 hours.
- Prepare a commitment tracker with owners/date targets for each corrective action.

I attached a working folder (will push a draft).

—Naomi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700

Subject: Aurora — draft RCA and proposed mitigations (internal draft)

Rajiv / team — attaching an internal draft of the RCA (aurora_rca_draft.pdf). This version contains:
- Timeline derived from request traces and autoscaler logs
- Evidence of a hot-shard KV-cache eviction pattern after a sudden spike of long-context requests
- Two short-term mitigations we executed (batch-size cap + temporary model-variant fallback) and their measured effect

We propose the following next steps for the exec readout:
1) Short exec summary slide (5–6 bullets)
2) Technical appendix (logs + latched traces) for your SREs
3) Commitment table with owners and dates (we'll deliver a tracker CSV)

Requested from Aurora: confirmation of the two windows when you observed customer-visible errors to correlate with our traces.

Attachments: aurora_rca_draft.pdf (internal draft), postmortem-appendix.csv (log extracts)

Thanks,
—Ben
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurora — draft RCA and proposed mitigations (internal draft)

Ben/Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround. We saw timeouts between 21:35–21:58 UTC and again at 22:47–22:58 UTC on 2027-04-07; our telemetry lines up with your traces. Helpful notes/questions:
- We need a clear commitment on SLA restoration and a list of observable checks we can run from our side during the canary.
- Our finance team is asking for a clear, itemized credit proposal to accelerate their internal signoff.

Would the draft credit be scoped as a one-time service credit tied to the hours of impact? Also, can you provide a short mitigation runbook we can include in our on-call playbook?

—Rajiv
Head of Infrastructure, Aurora Retail

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:51:00 -0700
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@auroraretail.com>, Aurora Ops Team <ops@auroraretail.com>, Anita Cheng <anita.cheng@auroraretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Aurora — draft RCA and proposed mitigations (customer-facing draft + commitments)

Rajiv / team — attaching the customer-facing RCA packet (summary + technical appendix) and a preliminary commitment tracker. Highlights below:
- Root cause (short): higher-than-expected long-context request mix hit an edge-case with our KV eviction heuristic on the 1.5B variant; this caused request replays and queue pressure on the embedding service.
- Immediate mitigations we ran: capped per-request batch size to 8 and rolled a compatible lower-KV-usage variant for 30 minutes which reduced 95th and 99th percentile latency by ~45%.
- Planned corrective actions (owner / target):
  * Production kernel patch to adjust KV eviction threshold — Ben / 2027-04-14
  * Canary rollout with manual gating + customer observability checks — Karthik / 2027-04-15
  * Post-deploy load test and validation report — Marissa / 2027-04-17
  * Credit proposal (one-time credit for incident window) — Laura / 2027-04-12

Attached: aurora_rca_final.pdf, commitment-tracker-sheet.csv (tracker is editable; we'll keep the sheet updated). The mitigation runbook section includes the observable checks (tail-latency, queue-depth, KV-miss-rate) you can run during canary.

Can you confirm whether the proposed dates and owners are acceptable? We'll lock the canary schedule once we have confirmation.

—Naomi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@auroraretail.com>
Subject: Re: Aurora — credit proposal and exec readout

All — I've reviewed the tracker and the proposed customer credit. I'm authorizing a one-time service credit equal to 40% of April's usage for the impacted routes (this is within our escalation guidelines for a multi-hour outage with executive engagement). Finance will draft the credit note; I asked them to use the DocuSign template (link below).

Please treat these as firm: kernel patch target 2027-04-14, canary no earlier than 2027-04-15, full deploy after validation on 2027-04-17. Karthik — own the canary schedule and share the observability dashboard link 24 hours in advance. Marissa — lead the load-test report and validate end-to-end checkout throughput.

Thanks — Laura
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
